title: Machine learning and cell experiments identify an SPP1 association with macrophages in pulmonary fibrosis
summary: Integrated machine-learning and single-cell analyses of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis datasets highlighted SPP1 and its expression in M2 macrophages. The study reports higher SPP1 in IPF lung tissue and in vitro experiments in which exogenous SPP1 reduced M2-macrophage migration and proliferation and increased apoptosis at some tested concentrations. The cell experiments are limited mechanistic evidence; they do not establish a causal disease mechanism or a clinical treatment effect, and the authors call for larger studies.
ai_technology: Machine-learning biomarker screening with integrated single-cell RNA sequencing

evidence.tested: The study combines dataset analyses and single-cell RNA sequencing with in vitro assays of exogenous SPP1 effects on M2 macrophage migration, proliferation, and apoptosis.
evidence.unknown: Cell-line experiments do not establish causality in human disease or clinical benefit; larger, well-designed experiments are needed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning analyses of IPF expression datasets helped prioritize candidate biomarkers, including SPP1, for subsequent cellular investigation.

source_review.scope: Full primary article text, including Methods, Results, author affiliations and publication history
